component.name: Simson Desk
component.summary: Email, calendar and tasks for Microsoft 365 and IMAP

description.p: Simson Desk is a desktop email, calendar and task client. It works with Microsoft 365, signing in with your Microsoft account, and with any mailbox that speaks IMAP and SMTP — Google Workspace, Zoho, Titan and most business hosts. It keeps a local copy of your mail so it stays fast and readable offline.
Features:

ul.li: Mail with conversation threading, rules, folders and multi-select
Calendar and Microsoft To Do tasks
Address book from your contacts, your organisation, and your own mail
Remote images blocked until you allow them, and links opened in your browser
Colour themes that can change by day or between working and off days
The local copy encrypted at rest, with the key in your system keyring
Locks itself when idle, and needs a fresh sign-in to reopen

description.p: Simson Desk is an independent client and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft.

screenshot.caption: Mail, with conversation threading and the reading pane

description.p: Inbox rules can be created again on Microsoft 365. Rules are kept under mailbox settings, which needs a permission separate from mail and was never being asked for, so every attempt was refused.
When a mailbox does withhold that permission, the app now says what is missing and what to do instead of showing the failed web address.
Importing an Outlook signature explains itself properly. It is unavailable in the Store build, and the message used to suggest a change that would have stopped personal Microsoft accounts signing in.
A quoted trail's embedded images are no longer listed as attachments, so a message with one spreadsheet shows one attachment rather than the signature logos beside it.
Writing a message no longer double-spaces. Paragraphs took the browser default margin, which put a blank line between every one.
The toolbars above the message list and around the reader are more compact, and the compose window no longer spends a third of its height on its own header.
Send now goes to the account the message is addressed from, rather than the one that happened to be selected.

Spell checking and the right-click menu are available while writing. Recipients can be added from an address-book dialog, and a name in a recipient box can be added to the address book by double-clicking it.
A signature keeps the colour the reply is written in, and is decided once rather than fighting itself as you type.
The reader shows the whole header, including Cc and Bcc, and it can be selected and copied.
Feedback can be sent from inside the app, and raised on the help desk where it will be answered. The app can check whether a newer version is available.
PDF previews render correctly and can be zoomed without going blurry.
The idle lock is off unless you turn it on, and never locks a window with no account signed in, which previously left no way back in.

Mail read or replied to on another device is no longer deleted from this app. A change notification carrying only the changed properties was mistaken for a deletion, which removed messages that were still on the server — replies and forwards most of all.
Microsoft 365 mail keeps syncing beyond the first hour. The access token was fixed at start-up and every request failed once it expired.
Marking a message read or flagged now reaches the server, so it shows in Outlook and stays that way.
The address book no longer fails entirely when an organisation withholds directory access; personal contacts still load.

Replies and forwards are marked in the list. Replies are saved to drafts while you type. Files pasted into a message are attached rather than pasted as a path, and images go inline. Double-click a message to read it full screen.
Signing in to a Microsoft 365 account works in the released build. It carried no Entra registration, so it asked every user to register an application of their own.
When Entra does refuse a sign-in, the app now says which setting is wrong instead of showing the raw error, and Settings can check the registration before opening a browser.
A separate signature for colleagues on your own domain, used for new messages, replies and forwards alike, and a button to insert a signature into a message that has none.
Inbox rules can forward arriving mail to another address.
Escape now closes the dialogs and the message window, saving a draft of anything you had typed.
New mail is announced on the desktop, and the inbox is checked every minute between full syncs rather than only on the sync interval.
Each mailbox now has its own folder tree, so a second account no longer merges into the first. Moving a message out of Spam works. Home and End open the first and last message in a folder.
Removing an account asks first, and says what it will delete.
Packaging only: the Windows Store build no longer asks for the restricted unvirtualizedResources capability, which testing showed it did not need. No change to the application itself.
Licensing change: Simson Desk is now proprietary software, licensed rather than sold. The About dialog and the supplied licence terms say so; no functional change accompanies it.
Mailboxes that are not Microsoft 365: any IMAP and SMTP server, including Google Workspace with an app password.

The local mail store is now encrypted at rest with SQLCipher, key held in the system keyring, attachments included. The application locks itself when left idle and needs a fresh sign-in to reopen, keeps a local activity log that records actions but never message content, and can discard its local copy of a mailbox on demand.
Signatures per sending address and per kind of message, in rich text. Address book with type-ahead recipients and @-mentions, theme palette with scheduled changes, and keyboard shortcuts throughout.
